Name: ArabMisinfo
Description: Arabic Facebook corpus for misinformation analysis.
Paper Title: ArabMisinfo: A Decade-Long Arabic Facebook Corpus for Misinformation Discourse and Engagement Analysis
Venue Name: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: IJCNLP-AACL 2026
Abstract: We present ArabMisinfo, a corpus of 274,837 public Facebook Page posts in Arabic spanning 2014–2024 and focused on news and public affairs. Each record includes page-level metadata, UTC timestamps, link domains, and platform-native engagement signals (likes, comments, shares, and the seven post-2016 reaction types). We accompany the corpus with reproducible diagnostics for engagement and polarization, the Polarization Index (PI), Share-to-Like Anomaly (SLA), Risk Triage Index (RTI), and Engagement Pattern Residuals (EPR). To address the absence of content-level labels, we contribute a discourse role annotation of 10,000 posts (3.6% of the corpus) using Fanar-C-2-27B, classifying each post into one of six roles. The annotation reveals that Arabic Facebook misinformation discourse is dominated by counter-information activity: 30.6% of posts are Rumor Denial or Official Correction, outpacing Unverified Claim posts (12.3%) by a 2.5:1 ratio, while 19.3% represent incidental keyword matches, directly quantifying the sampling noise introduced by keyword-based collection. To comply with platform terms and copyright, we publicly release Post IDs, Page IDs, and full metadata and derived indices; message text is available only under a research data-use agreement (DUA). ArabMisinfo enables engagement-aware analyses of Arabic misinformation ecosystems and, to our knowledge, provides the first discourse-role-annotated Arabic Facebook corpus at this scale.
